es: Distinguir en una negociación lo que alguien pide (postura) de lo que necesita (interés) y localizar el punto en común.

vocabulary.es: dispuesto a ceder, flexible en algo
carta de negociación, ficha de cambio

teaching.en: In a negotiation, a position is what you ask for, while an interest is the reason why you ask, and the reason is usually more flexible.
teaching.es: En una negociación, la postura es lo que pides, mientras que el interés es la razón por la que lo pides, y la razón suele ser más flexible.
teaching.explanationEs: Position = lo que exiges; interest = por qué lo exiges; flexible = que admite cambios.
segments: In a negotiation, a position is what you ask for, while an interest
is the reason why you ask, and the reason is usually more flexible.
teaching.audioText: In a negotiation, a position is what you ask for, while an interest is the reason why you ask, and the reason is usually more flexible.

teaching.en: The tenant's position is «lower the rent», but her underlying interest is to save money for her course and to stay in the flat for a long time.
teaching.es: La postura de la inquilina es «bajar el alquiler», pero su interés de fondo es ahorrar para su curso y quedarse en el piso mucho tiempo.
teaching.explanationEs: Underlying interest = la razón profunda, que a menudo no se dice al principio.
segments: The tenant's position is «lower the rent», but her underlying interest is to save
money for her course and to stay in the flat for a long time.
teaching.audioText: The tenant's position is «lower the rent», but her underlying interest is to save money for her course and to stay in the flat for a long time.

teaching.en: The seller's priority is a quick sale, so he is flexible about the price, but he will not give in to a buyer who wants to haggle all day.
teaching.es: La prioridad del vendedor es una venta rápida, así que es flexible con el precio, pero no cederá ante un comprador que quiera regatear todo el día.
teaching.explanationEs: Priority = lo que más importa; haggle = regatear el precio una y otra vez.
segments: The seller's priority is a quick sale, so he is flexible about the price, but
he will not give in to a buyer who wants to haggle all day.
teaching.audioText: The seller's priority is a quick sale, so he is flexible about the price, but he will not give in to a buyer who wants to haggle all day.

teaching.en: Two people who are entrenched in opposite positions often share the same interest, so it pays to ask why before you negotiate.
teaching.es: Dos personas atrincheradas en posturas opuestas a menudo comparten el mismo interés, así que conviene preguntar por qué antes de negociar.
teaching.explanationEs: Entrenched = aferrado a una postura; preguntar why abre la puerta a un acuerdo.
segments: Two people who are entrenched in opposite positions often share the
same interest, so it pays to ask why before you negotiate.
teaching.audioText: Two people who are entrenched in opposite positions often share the same interest, so it pays to ask why before you negotiate.

teaching.en: We both want a quiet flat, so we have common ground, and that gives us a solid base from which to negotiate.
teaching.es: Los dos queremos un piso tranquilo, así que tenemos un punto en común, y eso nos da una base sólida desde la que negociar.
teaching.explanationEs: Common ground es incontable: no lleva a ni plural.
segments: We both want a quiet flat, so we have common ground,
and that gives us a solid base from which to negotiate.
teaching.audioText: We both want a quiet flat, so we have common ground, and that gives us a solid base from which to negotiate.

teaching.en: Her stance is firm, but she has little leverage, because a bargaining chip such as a longer contract is the only thing she can offer.
teaching.es: Su postura es firme, pero tiene poco poder de presión, porque un argumento de cambio como un contrato más largo es lo único que puede ofrecer.
teaching.explanationEs: Leverage = poder para influir en el otro; bargaining chip = algo que ofreces a cambio.
segments: Her stance is firm, but she has little leverage, because a bargaining chip
such as a longer contract is the only thing she can offer.
teaching.audioText: Her stance is firm, but she has little leverage, because a bargaining chip such as a longer contract is the only thing she can offer.

prompt.es: Lee el intercambio. ¿Cuál es el interés de fondo de Tom?

choices.text: He wants to keep the car until the end of the year.
He wants to get the highest price of any seller in town.
He needs money for a course payment that is due soon.

feedback.es: «I need at least 4,500» es su postura; el interés de fondo es pagar el curso este mes. Las otras opciones no aparecen en el intercambio.

hint.es: La postura es la cifra que exige; el interés es la razón que da después de because.

origin.text: Ana wants to buy Tom's second-hand car, and she says: «I will not pay more than 4,000 dollars.» Tom answers: «I need at least 4,500, because I must pay for my course this month.»

prompt.es: Completa: «Su interés de fondo es conservar a un inquilino fiable durante varios años.»

feedback.es: Underlying interest nombra la razón profunda que hay detrás de lo que alguien pide.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo que significa «de fondo» y acompaña a interest.

origin.text: The landlord will not reduce the rent. That is his position, but his ___ interest is to keep a reliable tenant for several years.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Es flexible con la fecha, pero no con el precio.»

answer.text: She is flexible about the date but not about the price

feedback.es: Flexible about + nombre indica en qué puntos se puede ceder; la preposición habitual es about.

hint.es: Empieza con el sujeto y usa about para las dos cosas.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué punto en común descubren Leo y Mia.

choices.text: A short, cool and relaxed break close to water.
A long trip to the coast in late summer.
A week of visiting museums in a large city.

feedback.es: Descubren que lo que ambos buscan es un descanso corto, fresco y cerca del agua; la costa en agosto era solo la postura inicial de Mia.

origin.audio: Two friends were planning a holiday. Leo said that he refused to go to the coast in August, but when Mia asked him why, he explained that the heat gave him headaches and that he could not take more than a week off. Mia wanted the coast because she loved swimming. They discovered that they shared a real interest: a short, cool, relaxed break near water. So they agreed to look at a lake in the mountains in June, where Leo would be comfortable and Mia could swim.

prompt.es: Lee la negociación. ¿Qué carta de negociación utiliza el comprador?

choices.text: Offering to take the car without a service.
Offering to pay the whole price in one go today.
Promising to bring a friend who also wants a car.

feedback.es: El comprador ofrece pagar todo hoy («I pay the full price today»): es su bargaining chip, y con él consigue bajar el precio.

origin.text: Buyer: «I'll give you 4,000.» Seller: «I can't go below 4,600.» Buyer: «What if I pay the full price today?» Seller: «Then I could come down to 4,400 and include a full service.»

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el concepto de negociación que expresa.

pairs: I refuse to pay more than 400 dollars.

pairs.es: postura: lo que exijo

pairs: I must save money for my course.

pairs.es: interés: por qué lo pido

pairs: The date matters more to me than the price.

pairs.es: prioridad: lo que más importa

pairs: We both want a quiet flat.

pairs.es: punto en común

feedback.es: Cada frase expresa un concepto distinto: la postura exige, el interés explica, la prioridad ordena y el punto en común une.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato. ¿Qué interés de fondo tenía el casero?

choices.text: Finding a tenant who would take care of the flat.
Raising the rent every year for two years.
Covering a payment that would rise in July.

feedback.es: El casero admite que su pago al banco sube en julio: ese es su interés de fondo, no los 950 en sí.

origin.audio: Sara told me about her meeting with the landlord. He had insisted on a rent of 950, and she had refused to pay more than 850. Neither of them moved for ten minutes. Then she asked why 950 mattered so much, and he admitted that his bank payment goes up in July. She explained that she needed a stable home for two years because she was starting a course that lasts that long. In the end, they agreed on 900 for a two-year contract.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez. ¿Qué da a entender el acuerdo final sobre la forma de negociar?

choices.text: That asking about reasons helped each side get what it needed.
That the landlord was lying about his bank payment.
That the tenant won by refusing to move for ten minutes.

feedback.es: El acuerdo llega cuando preguntan por las razones: contrato de dos años para ella y un ingreso más seguro para él, no cuando alguien cede por cansancio.

origin.audio: Sara told me about her meeting with the landlord. He had insisted on a rent of 950, and she had refused to pay more than 850. Neither of them moved for ten minutes. Then she asked why 950 mattered so much, and he admitted that his bank payment goes up in July. She explained that she needed a stable home for two years because she was starting a course that lasts that long. In the end, they agreed on 900 for a two-year contract.

prompt.es: Completa: «El interés de la otra persona puede ser más flexible que su postura.»

feedback.es: Position e interest son opuestos complementarios: la postura es rígida, pero el interés de fondo suele ser flexible.

origin.text: Buyers who start with a fixed price often become entrenched. It is better to ask questions, because the other person's ___ may be more flexible than their position.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Nuestra prioridad es vender rápido, así que podemos negociar el precio.»

answer.text: Our priority is a quick sale so we can negotiate the price

feedback.es: Priority nombra lo que más importa; si es la rapidez, el precio pasa a ser negociable.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato. ¿Qué convirtió la discusión en un acuerdo?

choices.text: Tom giving up his study for good.
Asking about the need behind the demand.
Sara promising never to watch television.

feedback.es: Cuando Sara pregunta para qué necesita Tom la sala, aparece su interés real (trabajar tres mañanas) y es posible repartir el uso.

origin.audio: Tom and Sara were arguing about the living room. Tom wanted to keep it as a study, but Sara wanted a sofa and a television there. After a while, Sara asked him what he actually needed the room for, and Tom said that he only needed a quiet place to work three mornings a week. That changed the conversation completely: they agreed that Tom would use the room until noon on those mornings and that Sara could have her television in the afternoon.

prompt.es: Lee el diálogo. ¿Cuál es el interés de fondo de quien habla?

choices.text: To keep the car only for her own use, every weekend.
To avoid taking the bus on every weekend trip.
To be able to visit her mother without a long trip.

feedback.es: La negativa a compartir el coche es la postura; lo que necesita es llegar fácilmente hasta su madre. «Not necessarily the car» lo confirma.

origin.text: «I refuse to share the car at weekends.» «Why is that a problem?» «Because I visit my mother every Saturday, and the bus takes three hours.» «So what you need is a way to reach her, not necessarily the car.»

prompt.es: Completa: «Los dos queremos un piso tranquilo, así que tenemos un punto en común.»

feedback.es: Common ground es la expresión fija para el punto de acuerdo entre dos personas; es incontable.

origin.text: We disagree about the price. However, we both want a quiet flat, so we have common ___ to build on.

es: Convertir peticiones sueltas en propuestas de intercambio con in exchange for, on the understanding that e if you could…, we could….

vocabulary.es: sacrificar una cosa a cambio de otra
mejorar la oferta para que resulte atractiva

teaching.en: We are willing to sign for two years in exchange for a lower rent, because a long contract gives the landlord real security.
teaching.es: Estamos dispuestos a firmar dos años a cambio de un alquiler más bajo, porque un contrato largo da al propietario una seguridad real.
teaching.explanationEs: Be willing to + verbo muestra que cedes; in exchange for + nombre señala lo que recibes.
segments: We are willing to sign for two years in exchange for a
lower rent, because a long contract gives the landlord real security.
teaching.audioText: We are willing to sign for two years in exchange for a lower rent, because a long contract gives the landlord real security.

teaching.en: The landlord will waive the deposit on the understanding that the rent is paid on the first of each month, without any reminders.
teaching.es: El propietario renunciará al depósito con la condición de que el alquiler se pague el día uno de cada mes, sin recordatorios.
teaching.explanationEs: On the understanding that + cláusula con sujeto: condición que queda clara desde el principio.
segments: The landlord will waive the deposit on the understanding that the rent
is paid on the first of each month, without any reminders.
teaching.audioText: The landlord will waive the deposit on the understanding that the rent is paid on the first of each month, without any reminders.

teaching.en: If you could include parking, we could accept the whole package, which already covers the lower rent and the longer contract.
teaching.es: Si pudieras incluir el aparcamiento, podríamos aceptar todo el paquete, que ya recoge el alquiler más bajo y el contrato más largo.
teaching.explanationEs: If you could…, we could… es una propuesta suave y condicional; package = conjunto de peticiones.
segments: If you could include parking, we could accept the whole package,
which already covers the lower rent and the longer contract.
teaching.audioText: If you could include parking, we could accept the whole package, which already covers the lower rent and the longer contract.

teaching.en: I am willing to move my holiday dates if you reciprocate by paying for the hotel, so that neither of us loses out.
teaching.es: Estoy dispuesto a cambiar mis fechas de vacaciones si tú correspondes pagando el hotel, de modo que ninguno de los dos salga perdiendo.
teaching.explanationEs: Reciprocate = devolver un gesto con otro equivalente.
segments: I am willing to move my holiday dates if you reciprocate by
paying for the hotel, so that neither of us loses out.
teaching.audioText: I am willing to move my holiday dates if you reciprocate by paying for the hotel, so that neither of us loses out.

teaching.en: Try to bundle several small requests into one offer, because a neat bundle can sweeten the deal more than one big demand.
teaching.es: Intenta agrupar varias peticiones pequeñas en una sola oferta, porque un paquete bien armado puede mejorar el trato más que una gran exigencia.
teaching.explanationEs: Bundle = agrupar; sweeten the deal = hacer la oferta más atractiva para la otra parte.
segments: Try to bundle several small requests into one offer, because a
neat bundle can sweeten the deal more than one big demand.
teaching.audioText: Try to bundle several small requests into one offer, because a neat bundle can sweeten the deal more than one big demand.

teaching.en: A stipulation is a condition that must be met, and good negotiations rely on give and take, so each side has to trade off one demand against another.
teaching.es: Una condición exigida (stipulation) debe cumplirse, y las buenas negociaciones se basan en ceder por ambas partes, así que cada lado debe sacrificar una exigencia para ganar otra.
teaching.explanationEs: Stipulation = requisito; give and take = concesiones mutuas; trade off = renunciar a algo a cambio de otra cosa.
segments: A stipulation is a condition that must be met, and good negotiations rely on
give and take, so each side has to trade off one demand against another.
teaching.audioText: A stipulation is a condition that must be met, and good negotiations rely on give and take, so each side has to trade off one demand against another.

prompt.es: Elige la propuesta de intercambio que une las dos peticiones.

choices.text: We are willing to sign for three years in exchange for a lower rent.
We are willing to sign for three years in exchange of a lower rent.
We are willing to sign for three years on the understanding to pay less.

feedback.es: «In exchange for» es la fórmula correcta para un intercambio; «in exchange of» es un calco y «understanding to pay» no lleva that + cláusula.

hint.es: Busca la fórmula con for; on the understanding necesita that + sujeto.

origin.text: The tenant asks for a lower rent. The landlord asks for a longer contract. They want to turn these two separate requests into one offer.

prompt.es: Completa: «Renunciará al depósito con la condición de que se pague el día uno.»

feedback.es: On the understanding that + cláusula es la fórmula fija para fijar una condición.

hint.es: Es la preposición que abre la fórmula on the understanding that.

origin.text: The landlord wants the rent on time every month. He will waive the deposit ___ the understanding that the rent is paid on the first.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Si pudieras pagar antes de marzo, podríamos aceptar el paquete.»

answer.text: If you could pay by March we could accept the package

feedback.es: If you could…, we could… forma una propuesta suave: condición con could y resultado con could.

hint.es: Empieza con la condición y la coma separa el resultado.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué ofrece Tom a cambio del descuento.

choices.text: A payment on the first of every month.
A commitment to stay for two years.
The work of painting the kitchen himself.

feedback.es: Tom ofrece firmar dos años; pagar el día uno es la condición de Sara y pintar la cocina lo hará ella.

origin.audio: Tom and Sara spent an hour negotiating a new rental contract. At first, Tom asked for a lower rent and Sara asked for a longer contract. Then Tom suggested a package: he was willing to sign for two years in exchange for a five per cent discount, on the understanding that Sara would paint the kitchen. Sara thought for a moment and answered that she could accept it if Tom could pay on the first of every month. Tom agreed, and the deal was settled.

prompt.es: Completa: «A cambio de un contrato más largo, bajará el alquiler un diez por ciento.»

feedback.es: In exchange for + nombre expresa lo que se da a cambio de otra cosa.

origin.text: We need to keep the flat, and the owner needs a reliable tenant. ___ exchange for a longer contract, he will lower the rent by ten per cent.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fórmula con la función que cumple en una propuesta.

pairs.es: señala lo que recibes a cambio
fija una condición clara
plantea una oferta suave y condicional
muestra que estás dispuesto a ceder

feedback.es: Cada fórmula tiene su función: el intercambio, la condición, la oferta suave y la disposición a ceder.

pairs.es: señala lo que recibes a cambio
fija una condición clara
plantea una oferta suave y condicional
muestra que estás dispuesto a ceder

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de Sara. ¿Qué condición pone para renunciar al depósito?

choices.text: That the contract lasts for at least two years.
That Tom pays the extra fifty dollars in full today.
That the rent arrives by the first of every month.

feedback.es: Sara renunciará al depósito «on the understanding that you pay by the first of each month»; los dos años los acepta desde el principio y nadie habla de pagar en efectivo.

origin.audio: Hi Tom, it's Sara. I have thought about your offer, and I like the idea of a two-year contract. However, the rent you suggest is a little too low for me. Here is what I can do: I will waive the deposit on the understanding that you pay by the first of each month, and if you could look after the garden, we could settle at nine hundred and fifty. Let me know whether that package works for you before Friday.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez. ¿Qué da a entender Sara sobre su actitud ante la oferta?

choices.text: That she is open to a deal, but wants some changes.
That she has already rejected the offer for good.
That she will accept anything for a two-year contract.

feedback.es: Le gusta la idea del contrato de dos años, pero el alquiler es bajo y propone su propia versión: está abierta al trato con cambios.

origin.audio: Hi Tom, it's Sara. I have thought about your offer, and I like the idea of a two-year contract. However, the rent you suggest is a little too low for me. Here is what I can do: I will waive the deposit on the understanding that you pay by the first of each month, and if you could look after the garden, we could settle at nine hundred and fifty. Let me know whether that package works for you before Friday.

prompt.es: Completa: «Estoy dispuesto a cambiar mis fechas si tú me devuelves el gesto.»

feedback.es: Be willing to + verbo muestra que estás dispuesto a ceder sin sonar débil.

origin.text: Tom wants to show that he can give something up. He says: «I am ___ to move my holiday dates if you pay for the hotel.»

prompt.es: Elige la frase con un error de patrón.

choices.text: We will waive the deposit on the understanding that you pay early.
In exchange of a longer contract, we will lower the rent.
If you could include parking, we could accept the package.

feedback.es: «In exchange of» es un calco: la fórmula correcta es in exchange for; las otras dos frases siguen bien el patrón.

prompt.es: Escucha el resumen de la directora. ¿Qué da a entender su última frase?

choices.text: That nobody will be allowed to leave the company.
That the company will pay half of the cost anyway.
That refusing the package would mean losing the courses.

feedback.es: «The alternative was no courses at all» implica que quien rechace el paquete se queda sin cursos, aunque nadie esté obligado.

origin.audio: After a long meeting, the manager summarised the deal. The company would pay for the language courses in exchange for staff staying at least two years. Employees could leave earlier, but only if they paid back half of the cost. She added that nobody was forced to accept, yet the alternative was no courses at all.

prompt.es: ¿Qué ofrece el inquilino a cambio de que se renuncie al depósito?

choices.text: The first three months of rent, paid in advance.
A contract of one year at a lower rent.
A decision on the same day he replies.

feedback.es: A cambio de que renuncien al depósito, ofrece pagar los tres primeros meses por adelantado; el contrato de un año mantiene el alquiler igual.

origin.text: Thanks for your message. We could accept a shorter contract of one year on the understanding that the rent stays the same. If you could also waive the deposit, we could sign this week. In return, we are willing to pay the first three months in advance.

prompt.es: Completa: «Las buenas negociaciones se basan en ceder ambas partes.»

feedback.es: Give and take es la expresión fija para las concesiones mutuas.

origin.text: Nobody gets everything they want. Good negotiations rely on give and ___, so that each side concedes something.

es: Seguir una negociación oída o leída y registrar las ofertas, las condiciones y la firmeza de cada compromiso.

teaching.en: In principle, I can agree to 900 dollars, but that is only tentative until I have spoken to my partner about the repairs.
teaching.es: En principio puedo aceptar 900 dólares, pero es solo provisional hasta que hable con mi socio sobre las reparaciones.
teaching.explanationEs: In principle y tentative avisan de que todavía no hay acuerdo firme.
segments: In principle, I can agree to 900 dollars, but that is only
tentative until I have spoken to my partner about the repairs.
teaching.audioText: In principle, I can agree to 900 dollars, but that is only tentative until I have spoken to my partner about the repairs.

teaching.en: We can offer 900 dollars a month, subject to a two-year contract and to a short inspection of the flat before anyone signs.
teaching.es: Podemos ofrecer 900 dólares al mes, sujeto a un contrato de dos años y a una breve inspección del piso antes de firmar.
teaching.explanationEs: Subject to añade una condición previa: sin ella la oferta no se mantiene.
segments: We can offer 900 dollars a month, subject to a two-year contract
and to a short inspection of the flat before anyone signs.
teaching.audioText: We can offer 900 dollars a month, subject to a two-year contract and to a short inspection of the flat before anyone signs.

teaching.en: Let's meet halfway: I offer 950 and you fix the heating before the first of the month, so neither of us loses out.
teaching.es: Lleguemos a un punto medio: yo ofrezco 950 y tú arreglas la calefacción antes del día uno, de modo que ninguno salga perdiendo.
teaching.explanationEs: Meet halfway marca una concesión mutua: cada parte cede algo.
segments: Let's meet halfway: I offer 950 and you fix the heating before
the first of the month, so neither of us loses out.
teaching.audioText: Let's meet halfway: I offer 950 and you fix the heating before the first of the month, so neither of us loses out.

teaching.en: I cannot commit to that date yet, because the booking is only provisional, but I will firm up the details by Friday.
teaching.es: Todavía no puedo comprometerme con esa fecha, porque la reserva es solo provisional, pero concretaré los detalles para el viernes.
teaching.explanationEs: Commit to + nombre o -ing expresa un compromiso real; firm up convierte lo provisional en firme.
segments: I cannot commit to that date yet, because the booking is
only provisional, but I will firm up the details by Friday.
teaching.audioText: I cannot commit to that date yet, because the booking is only provisional, but I will firm up the details by Friday.

teaching.en: Once we both sign the contract, it is binding, so read every caveat carefully, because a small condition can change the whole deal.
teaching.es: Una vez que los dos firmemos el contrato, será vinculante, así que lee cada salvedad con atención, porque una condición pequeña puede cambiar todo el trato.
teaching.explanationEs: Binding = que obliga legalmente; caveat = salvedad que limita lo prometido.
segments: Once we both sign the contract, it is binding, so read every
caveat carefully, because a small condition can change the whole deal.
teaching.audioText: Once we both sign the contract, it is binding, so read every caveat carefully, because a small condition can change the whole deal.

teaching.en: The offer is still pending, since the owner has not replied, so nothing is agreed and we should not treat the price as final.
teaching.es: La oferta sigue pendiente, porque el propietario no ha contestado, así que nada está acordado y no debemos tratar el precio como definitivo.
teaching.explanationEs: Pending = a la espera de respuesta o de una decisión.
segments: The offer is still pending, since the owner has not replied, so
nothing is agreed and we should not treat the price as final.
teaching.audioText: The offer is still pending, since the owner has not replied, so nothing is agreed and we should not treat the price as final.

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje. ¿Cómo de firme es el compromiso de Carlos?

choices.text: Firm: he has already accepted the price of 900 in writing.
Not firm: it depends on seeing the list of repairs.
Cancelled: he refuses to talk about the price of the flat.

feedback.es: «In principle» y «only tentative» indican que no es firme y depende de ver la lista de reparaciones; tampoco ha firmado ni ha rechazado hablar del precio.

hint.es: Fíjate en las palabras que avisan de que el acuerdo aún no es firme.

origin.text: Carlos wrote: «In principle, I can accept 900, but that is only tentative until I have seen the list of repairs, and I will not sign anything before then.»

prompt.es: Completa: «Hasta que firmemos, el acuerdo no es vinculante.»

feedback.es: Binding describe un compromiso que obliga de verdad, normalmente tras la firma.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo para un acuerdo que obliga legalmente.

origin.text: We have not signed anything yet. Until we do, the agreement is not ___, and either of us can still walk away.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Puedo comprometerme con el precio, pero no con la fecha.»

answer.text: I can commit to the price but not to the date

feedback.es: Commit to + nombre: cada compromiso lleva su propia preposición to.

hint.es: Repite commit to para el precio y la fecha.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige de qué depende que la inquilina se comprometa a dos años.

choices.text: Of the rent falling below 900 dollars.
Of his partner signing the contract.
Of the heating being repaired first.

feedback.es: Ella solo se compromete a dos años si antes arreglan la calefacción; la aprobación de la pareja del casero condiciona el acuerdo de él, no el compromiso de ella.

origin.audio: The tenant called the landlord to discuss next year's rent. The landlord said that, in principle, he could accept 900 dollars a month, subject to a two-year contract. The tenant replied that she could commit to two years only if the heating was repaired first. The landlord thought about it, then offered a solution: he would repair the heating in October, and she would sign in September. They agreed to meet halfway, but he warned that his agreement was provisional until his partner approved it.

prompt.es: Completa: «La aceptación del casero está sujeta a que su socio diga que sí.»

feedback.es: Subject to añade una condición previa: sin el sí del socio, no hay aceptación.

origin.text: Both sides have made offers, but nothing is final. The landlord's acceptance is ___ to his partner saying yes.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con lo que indica sobre el acuerdo.

pairs.es: provisional, sin confirmar
obliga a las dos partes
de acuerdo en general, sin cerrar detalles
cada parte cede algo

feedback.es: Estas expresiones miden cuán firme es un acuerdo: provisional, vinculante, general o fruto de concesiones mutuas.

prompt.es: Escucha la llamada. ¿A qué se compromete Mia y con qué condición?

choices.text: To two years, if the heating is repaired before October.
To two years, whatever happens with the heating in the flat.
To one year, unless the price falls to 850 a month.

feedback.es: Mia se compromete a dos años solo si se repara la calefacción antes de octubre; no dice que lo haría pase lo que pase ni habla de bajar a 850.

origin.audio: Mia phoned Carlos to discuss her rental contract. Carlos began by saying that he could agree to 900 a month in principle, but that the figure was only tentative, because his partner had not seen it yet. Mia said she could commit to two years, if the heating was repaired before October. Carlos answered that he could not promise the repairs for October, only for the end of November. They finally agreed to meet halfway: the repairs would be done by the middle of November, and the contract would be signed only after that.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez. ¿Qué muestra el acuerdo final sobre la fecha de las reparaciones?

choices.text: That Mia obtained exactly the date she had wanted.
That both sides moved away from their first date.
That Carlos will repair the heating before October.

feedback.es: Mia quería antes de octubre y Carlos a finales de noviembre: acuerdan mediados de noviembre, es decir, cada uno cede.

origin.audio: Mia phoned Carlos to discuss her rental contract. Carlos began by saying that he could agree to 900 a month in principle, but that the figure was only tentative, because his partner had not seen it yet. Mia said she could commit to two years, if the heating was repaired before October. Carlos answered that he could not promise the repairs for October, only for the end of November. They finally agreed to meet halfway: the repairs would be done by the middle of November, and the contract would be signed only after that.

prompt.es: Completa: «La oferta sigue pendiente hasta que responda la pareja del dueño.»

feedback.es: Pending describe algo a la espera de una respuesta o decisión.

origin.text: Nothing has been signed. The offer is still ___ until the owner's partner has replied.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El acuerdo es provisional hasta que mi socio lo apruebe.»

answer.text: The agreement is provisional until my partner approves it

feedback.es: Provisional marca que el acuerdo todavía no es definitivo; until + presente indica cuándo dejará de serlo.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de Tom. ¿Qué pide Tom a la propietaria?

choices.text: A lower price for the second week of August.
Permission to bring two more friends along.
Time to confirm the dates before he commits.

feedback.es: Tom pide que le guarde el piso hasta el viernes para poder concretar la reserva cuando sepa las fechas de sus amigos.

origin.audio: Hello, this is Tom. About the holiday flat: in principle, we would like to book it for the second week of August, but we cannot commit yet, because two of our friends are still waiting for their holidays to be confirmed. Could you hold the flat until Friday without a deposit? If you can, I will firm up the booking as soon as I know. Otherwise, I understand that you must offer it to someone else.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la autora sobre su compromiso?

choices.text: That she will not be bound until both items arrive.
That she has already signed and is only checking the details.
That she will reject the contract after the inspection.

feedback.es: Su acuerdo es provisional hasta recibir la lista de reparaciones y el precio depende de la inspección: no quedará obligada hasta entonces.

origin.text: Dear Ms Lee, thank you for the contract. Please note that my agreement is provisional until the list of repairs is attached, and that the price is subject to the final inspection. Once I receive both, I will be happy to sign.

prompt.es: Completa: «Se encontrarán a medio camino: él baja el precio y ella acepta más tiempo.»

feedback.es: Meet halfway es la expresión para llegar a un punto medio mediante concesiones mutuas.

origin.text: Neither side will get everything. They will meet ___: he lowers the price a little, and she accepts a longer contract.

es: Formular concesiones condicionadas y contraofertas con provided that, as long as, unless y otherwise en una negociación de ocho turnos.

teaching.en: I can concede the parking place, provided that you pay the deposit this week, but I will not budge on the monthly price.
teaching.es: Puedo ceder la plaza de aparcamiento, siempre que pagues el depósito esta semana, pero no me moveré del precio mensual.
teaching.explanationEs: Concede + provided that + condición en presente; budge = mover(se) de una postura.
segments: I can concede the parking place, provided that you pay the deposit
this week, but I will not budge on the monthly price.
teaching.audioText: I can concede the parking place, provided that you pay the deposit this week, but I will not budge on the monthly price.

teaching.en: I will concede a fixed rent for next year as long as you stay for two years, and the whole arrangement is contingent on a signed contract by Friday.
teaching.es: Concederé un alquiler fijo para el año próximo mientras te quedes dos años, y todo el acuerdo está condicionado a un contrato firmado para el viernes.
teaching.explanationEs: As long as + presente; contingent on + nombre: algo depende de otra cosa.
segments: I will concede a fixed rent for next year as long as you stay for
two years, and the whole arrangement is contingent on a signed contract by Friday.
teaching.audioText: I will concede a fixed rent for next year as long as you stay for two years, and the whole arrangement is contingent on a signed contract by Friday.

teaching.en: We will not sign unless the heating is repaired, and if you refuse, we will stand firm until you reconsider your answer.
teaching.es: No firmaremos a menos que se repare la calefacción, y si te niegas, nos mantendremos firmes hasta que reconsideres tu respuesta.
teaching.explanationEs: Unless ya significa «si no»: no se añade otra negación; stand firm = no ceder.
segments: We will not sign unless the heating is repaired, and if
you refuse, we will stand firm until you reconsider your answer.
teaching.audioText: We will not sign unless the heating is repaired, and if you refuse, we will stand firm until you reconsider your answer.

teaching.en: Pay on the first of the month; otherwise, we will review the contract, and I will not give ground a second time.
teaching.es: Paga el día uno de cada mes; de lo contrario, revisaremos el contrato, y no volveré a ceder terreno una segunda vez.
teaching.explanationEs: Otherwise avisa de la consecuencia si no se cumple; give ground = ceder terreno.
segments: Pay on the first of the month; otherwise, we will review
the contract, and I will not give ground a second time.
teaching.audioText: Pay on the first of the month; otherwise, we will review the contract, and I will not give ground a second time.

teaching.en: That is too high, so here is my counteroffer: 880 a month, with the deposit in two parts, and I will hold out for that figure.
teaching.es: Eso es demasiado alto, así que aquí va mi contraoferta: 880 al mes, con el depósito en dos partes, y resistiré hasta conseguir esa cifra.
teaching.explanationEs: Counteroffer = nueva propuesta ante una oferta que no te sirve; hold out for = esperar sin aceptar menos.
segments: That is too high, so here is my counteroffer: 880 a month, with
the deposit in two parts, and I will hold out for that figure.
teaching.audioText: That is too high, so here is my counteroffer: 880 a month, with the deposit in two parts, and I will hold out for that figure.

teaching.en: Threatening to leave is an ultimatum, and an ultimatum closes the door, whereas a conditional concession keeps the conversation open.
teaching.es: Amenazar con irse es un ultimátum, y un ultimátum cierra la puerta, mientras que una concesión condicionada mantiene abierta la conversación.
teaching.explanationEs: Ultimatum = «o lo tomas o lo dejas»; una concesión condicionada cede, pero con condición.
segments: Threatening to leave is an ultimatum, and an ultimatum closes
the door, whereas a conditional concession keeps the conversation open.
teaching.audioText: Threatening to leave is an ultimatum, and an ultimatum closes the door, whereas a conditional concession keeps the conversation open.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que funciona como contraoferta.

choices.text: I refuse to pay 400, and that is my last word on the subject.
I will pay 300; otherwise, you can find another tenant for your hall.
Here is my counteroffer: 350 dollars, and we clean the hall after every market.

feedback.es: Una contraoferta ofrece una cifra nueva con sus condiciones; las otras dos frases son un rechazo cerrado y un ultimátum.

hint.es: Busca la frase que propone una cifra distinta y algo a cambio.

origin.text: Leo wants 400 dollars a month for the hall, but Ana can only pay 300. She decides to make a proposal instead of simply saying no.

prompt.es: Completa: «No firmaremos a menos que se repare antes la calefacción.»

feedback.es: Unless significa «a menos que» y ya contiene la negación: no se añade don't.

hint.es: Es la conjunción que equivale a «si no».

origin.text: The heating is broken and the landlord has not repaired it. We will not sign ___ the heating is repaired first.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Aceptaré 350 siempre que limpies la sala.»

answer.text: I will accept 350 as long as you clean the hall

feedback.es: As long as + presente fija la condición de la concesión: aceptar 350 depende de limpiar la sala.

hint.es: La condición va con as long as y el verbo en presente, no en futuro.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué condición pone Sara para firmar.

choices.text: That the whole agreement is written down before signing.
That Tom pays all the bills himself.
That the big room is hers for ever.

feedback.es: Sara dice que no firmará «unless it was in writing»: su condición es dejarlo todo por escrito; pagar las facturas a tiempo era la condición de Tom.

origin.audio: Sara and Tom were negotiating the use of the big room in their flat. Tom conceded the room on one condition: Sara would pay the bills on time; otherwise, he would ask for it back. Sara accepted, but she refused to pay for the internet alone, so she made a counteroffer: they would share it equally, as long as Tom agreed to write everything down. Tom did not budge at first, but when Sara said she would not sign unless it was in writing, he agreed.

prompt.es: Completa: «Paga el depósito esta semana; si no, ofreceré la habitación a otro.»

feedback.es: Otherwise avisa de la consecuencia si la condición no se cumple.

origin.text: The room is in demand. Pay the deposit this week; ___, I will offer the room to somebody else.

la concesión se mantiene salvo que ocurra algo

feedback.es: Cada palabra cumple un papel distinto: condición, excepción, consecuencia y nueva propuesta.

choices.text: That Ana has the keys on Friday evenings.
That Ana pays for the cleaning herself.
That Ana calls back before Wednesday.

feedback.es: Leo baja a 350 «provided that she pay for the cleaning herself»; las llaves del viernes son lo que pide Ana y lo de llamar el miércoles es lo que ella promete.

origin.audio: Leo phoned Ana about the hall. He said that he could lower the rent to 350, provided that she pay for the cleaning herself. Ana said the price was acceptable as long as she had the keys on Friday evenings. Leo could not promise that, because a choir used the hall until nine on Fridays, so he suggested Saturday mornings instead. Ana was not happy, yet she did not want an ultimatum: she answered that she would think about it and call him back by Wednesday.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez. ¿Qué actitud adopta Ana ante los sábados por la mañana?

choices.text: Happy, since it solves her problem at last.
Angry, and ready to end the talks there.
Reluctant, but still willing to keep on talking.

feedback.es: No está contenta, pero no quiere un ultimátum: dice que lo pensará y responderá el miércoles.

origin.audio: Leo phoned Ana about the hall. He said that he could lower the rent to 350, provided that she pay for the cleaning herself. prompt.es: Completa: «Mejor una contraoferta que mantenga viva la conversación.»

feedback.es: Una contraoferta propone algo distinto sin cerrar la conversación, a diferencia del ultimátum.

origin.text: Saying «take it or leave it» is an ultimatum. A better strategy is to make a ___ that keeps the conversation going.

prompt.es: Escribe un diálogo de ocho turnos con dos concesiones condicionadas y una contraoferta.

answer.text: Ana: Hello, Leo. I would like to rent your hall on Saturdays for a small market. I can offer 300 dollars a month. Leo: That is too low. I need 400, because I pay for heating and cleaning every week. Ana: I understand. Here is my counteroffer: 350 dollars, and we clean the hall after every market. Leo: I can accept 350 as long as you clean it before six in the evening, and I will not budge on that. Ana: Agreed, provided that you give us the keys on Friday night. Leo: I will give you the keys unless there is a private party on Saturday morning. Ana: That is fair, but please tell me by Thursday; otherwise, we will plan the first market for next month. Leo: Deal. I will send you a written agreement tomorrow, and you can sign it on Saturday.
accepted: Ana: Hello, Leo. I would like to rent your hall on Saturdays for a small market. I can offer 300 dollars a month. Leo: That is too low. I need 400, because I pay for heating and cleaning every week. Ana: I understand. Here is my counteroffer: 350 dollars, and we clean the hall after every market. Leo: I can accept 350 as long as you clean it before six in the evening, and I will not budge on that. Ana: Agreed, provided that you give us the keys on Friday night. Leo: I will give you the keys unless there is a private party on Saturday morning. Ana: That is fair, but please tell me by Thursday; otherwise, we will plan the first market for next month. Leo: Deal. I will send you a written agreement tomorrow, and you can sign it on Saturday.

Ana: Good morning. I am interested in your hall for a weekend market, and I can offer 300 dollars a month. Leo: Thank you, but that does not cover my costs. My price is 400. Ana: Let me make a counteroffer: 340 dollars, provided that we may use the kitchen. Leo: You can use the kitchen as long as everything is clean when you leave. Ana: Of course. We will also pay on the first of each month unless you prefer a different day. Leo: The first is perfect, but I need the money on time; otherwise, I will have to raise the price. Ana: Then we agree: 340 a month, kitchen included, clean before six. Leo: Deal. I will write it down tonight, and we can both sign it on Saturday.

feedback.es: El diálogo debe alternar oferta, contraoferta y concesiones con provided that, as long as o unless, y cerrar con un acuerdo.

origin.text: Ana quiere alquilar el salón de Leo los sábados para un mercadillo. Ana ofrece 300 dólares al mes y Leo pide 400. Escribe en inglés un diálogo de ocho turnos (Ana y Leo, entre 140 y 240 palabras) con dos concesiones condicionadas (provided that, as long as o unless), una contraoferta y un cierre de acuerdo.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato. ¿Qué sugiere que la inquilina pida la oferta por escrito?

choices.text: That she is seriously considering it but will not commit straight away.
That she has accepted the offer and only needs a receipt for it.
That she no longer wants a lower rent at all, after the offer.

feedback.es: Pedir la oferta por escrito en vez de contestar indica que la estudia, pero no se compromete todavía.

origin.audio: During the meeting, the tenant said that she would hold out for a lower rent, because the heating had been broken for a month. The landlord refused to give ground on the price, yet he offered to pay for a new heating system, provided that she signed for two more years. She did not answer immediately. Instead, she asked for the offer in writing.

prompt.es: ¿Qué función cumple la última frase del correo?

choices.text: It cancels the counteroffer that was made a moment earlier.
It warns what will happen if the deadline is missed.
It adds a second, higher price to the counteroffer of 880.

feedback.es: Tras otherwise se anuncia la consecuencia de no firmar para el viernes: ofrecerán el piso a otra familia.

origin.text: Dear Ms Green, I am afraid that I cannot accept your first offer, but I do not want to reject it entirely. Our counteroffer is 880 a month, with the deposit paid in two parts. This proposal is contingent on a signed contract by Friday; otherwise, we will have to offer the flat to another family.

prompt.es: Completa: «No cederá en el precio, pero está dispuesto a hablar de la fecha.»

feedback.es: Budge on + nombre significa moverse de una postura; suele usarse en negativa.

origin.text: The landlord will not ___ on the price, but he is willing to discuss the date of the move.

es: Negociar las reglas y los gastos de un piso compartido expresando intereses, cediendo con condiciones y confirmando por escrito lo acordado.

teaching.en: Just to recap, we will split the utilities equally, and Tom will pay the internet, which we will itemise on a shared sheet every month.
teaching.es: Solo para resumir, repartiremos los suministros a partes iguales, y Tom pagará el internet, que detallaremos en una hoja compartida cada mes.
teaching.explanationEs: Recap abre el resumen; split = repartir; itemise = detallar cada gasto por separado.
segments: Just to recap, we will split the utilities equally, and Tom will pay
the internet, which we will itemise on a shared sheet every month.
teaching.audioText: Just to recap, we will split the utilities equally, and Tom will pay the internet, which we will itemise on a shared sheet every month.

teaching.en: As discussed, the cleaning rota starts on Monday and changes every week, so nobody has to do the bathroom twice in a row.
teaching.es: Como hablamos, el turno de limpieza empieza el lunes y cambia cada semana, así que nadie tiene que limpiar el baño dos veces seguidas.
teaching.explanationEs: As discussed remite a lo hablado; rota = cuadrante de turnos.
segments: As discussed, the cleaning rota starts on Monday and changes every week,
so nobody has to do the bathroom twice in a row.
teaching.audioText: As discussed, the cleaning rota starts on Monday and changes every week, so nobody has to do the bathroom twice in a row.

teaching.en: I am writing to confirm what we agreed in the meeting, and I would like the main points in writing before anyone signs the contract.
teaching.es: Te escribo para confirmar lo que acordamos en la reunión, y quisiera tener los puntos principales por escrito antes de que nadie firme el contrato.
teaching.explanationEs: Confirm = dejar cerrado lo acordado; in writing = por escrito, como prueba.
segments: I am writing to confirm what we agreed in the meeting, and I
would like the main points in writing before anyone signs the contract.

teaching.en: Please let me know in writing if anything is wrong, because any ambiguity now can easily become a misunderstanding later.

teaching.explanationEs: Ambiguity = algo que admite dos lecturas; se corrige antes de que cause un misunderstanding.
segments: Please let me know in writing if anything is wrong,

prompt.es: Lee el borrador de Mia. ¿Qué punto es una ambigüedad que debe aclararse?

choices.text: The length of a guest's stay is left unclear.
The day on which the rota begins is left unclear.
The way the bills are divided is left unclear.

feedback.es: «A few nights» no dice cuántas noches son; el lunes y el reparto igualitario sí están concretados.

hint.es: Busca la expresión que no da una cifra exacta.

feedback.es: Just to recap abre un resumen breve de lo acordado.

answer.text: Please let me know in writing if anything is wrong

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué propone Sara para evitar discusiones futuras.

choices.text: To ask Tom to pay all the electricity.
To list each cost on a shared sheet.
To hold the meeting again the next week.

feedback.es: Sara se ofrece a detallar los gastos en una hoja compartida para que nadie pueda decir después que las cifras no estaban claras.

origin.audio: Tom, Mia and Sara held a meeting to agree the ground rules of their flat. They decided to split the utilities equally, although Tom pointed out that he worked from home and would use more electricity. Mia suggested that he pay a slightly larger share, provided that he did not have to clean the kitchen. Everyone agreed, and Sara offered to itemise the costs on a shared sheet, so that nobody could claim later that the figures were unclear. The meeting ended on a friendly note.

prompt.es: ¿Qué detalle del mensaje puede provocar un malentendido?

choices.text: «On Monday» is too early for a rota to begin.
«In advance» shows that guests may never stay.
«As agreed» does not say how the bills are shared.

feedback.es: «As agreed» remite a algo sin repetirlo, y cada lector podría entender un reparto distinto; el lunes y las dos noches sí son precisos.

origin.text: Hi both, as discussed, the rota starts on Monday and guests may stay for two nights, provided that they tell everyone in advance. We will share the bills as agreed, and Mia will deal with the cleaning products.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una charla amistosa es posible cuando cada uno explica lo que necesita.»

feedback.es: Amicable describe una conversación o acuerdo cordial, sin hostilidad.

origin.text: Nobody wants a fight over money. A calm, ___ discussion is possible when each person explains what they really need.

prompt.es: Escucha la llamada. ¿Qué concede Mia y con qué condición?

choices.text: A later start for the rota, if Tom does the first two weeks.
A later start for the rota, whatever Tom decides to do.
An earlier start for the rota, if Tom passes his exams.

feedback.es: Mia acepta retrasar el turno hasta después de los exámenes, siempre que Tom haga las dos primeras semanas.

origin.audio: Mia and Tom were finalising the rules of the flat. Tom said he would accept the cleaning rota, as long as it started after the exams, because he would have no time before then. Mia did not like the delay, but she conceded it, provided that he took the first two weeks once the exams were over. They also agreed that guests could stay two nights, unless an exam was the next day, in which case the flat would be quiet. Before ending the call, Mia promised to write the whole deal down that evening.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez. ¿Qué sugiere la promesa final de Mia de escribirlo todo?

choices.text: That she suspects that Tom will change his mind soon.
That she wants to avoid future disagreements about the deal.
That she prefers writing because she cannot phone again.

feedback.es: Poner el acuerdo por escrito es la forma de evitar malentendidos después; el relato no insinúa desconfianza ni problemas para volver a llamar.

origin.audio: Mia and Tom were finalising the rules of the flat. Tom said he would accept the cleaning rota, as long as it started after the exams, because he would have no time before then. prompt.es: Completa: «Te escribo para confirmar lo que acordamos, y así evitar malentendidos.»

feedback.es: I am writing to confirm… es la apertura habitual de un mensaje que fija lo acordado.

origin.text: After the meeting, Mia sends a message: «I am writing to ___ what we agreed, so that there is no misunderstanding.»

prompt.es: Escribe el mensaje que confirma por escrito lo acordado en la reunión del piso.

answer.text: Hi Mia and Tom, I am writing to confirm what we agreed in the meeting. Just to recap, we will split the bills equally, Tom will pay the internet, and Mia will buy the cleaning products. The cleaning rota starts on Monday and changes every week. Guests may stay for two nights, provided that we tell each other in advance. As discussed, the deposit will be divided equally, and everybody will have paid it no later than the fifth. I would like to have all of this in writing, so there is no misunderstanding later. If anything is different from your notes, please reply today and I will correct it, because I want to avoid any ambiguity before we sign. Thanks for being so flexible. I think this is a fair package for all of us, and I am sure the flat will be a good place to live.

Dear both, here is a short summary of our meeting. To recap, each of us will pay a third of the bills, and Tom will take care of the internet in exchange for Mia buying the cleaning products. The rota for cleaning begins on Monday. We agreed that guests can stay for two nights as long as we warn the others beforehand. The deposit will be split equally, and we will have paid it by the fifth. Please check this message and let me know in writing if you see a misunderstanding. Otherwise, I will consider everything confirmed. I am really happy that we reached this agreement without any argument, and I look forward to living with you both, because this is a fair package for everybody in the flat and a good start for the year.

feedback.es: Un buen mensaje de confirmación resume lo pactado, repite las condiciones y pide corregir cualquier malentendido por escrito.

origin.text: Notas de la reunión del piso compartido: facturas a partes iguales; Tom paga el internet y Mia compra los productos de limpieza; turnos de limpieza desde el lunes; invitados hasta dos noches si se avisa con antelación; depósito dividido a partes iguales y pagado antes del día 5. Escribe en inglés un mensaje de confirmación de 150 a 260 palabras: resumen, condiciones y petición de corregir cualquier malentendido.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje. ¿Qué da a entender el final del mensaje de Sara?

choices.text: That she will change the rules after Friday.
That nobody will sign until all have replied.
That silence will be taken as a sign of agreement.

feedback.es: Si nadie responde antes del viernes, dará el mensaje por definitivo: el silencio cuenta como conformidad.

origin.audio: Sara's message was polite but firm. She thanked her flatmates for a productive meeting, then recapped three points: the bills would be split equally, the rota would start on Monday, and the deposit would be paid by the fifth. She ended by saying that she would treat the message as final unless someone replied by Friday.

prompt.es: ¿Por qué el mensaje A evita mejor un malentendido que el B?

choices.text: It states the points clearly and invites corrections.
It is longer and therefore sounds more serious.
It avoids mentioning the rota or the bills.

feedback.es: El mensaje A repite los puntos acordados y pide corregir por escrito; el B no fija nada concreto.

origin.text: Message A: «Hi, just to recap, we split the bills equally and the rota starts on Monday. Please tell me in writing if I have missed anything.» Message B: «Hi, as we said, everything is sorted. Nothing more to do. See you soon!»
